provenance: LLM-backend-derived (this session, no API key) + deterministic-checked — NOT a ship typology config. build_rec follows the cover×data matrix (build_rec_category); every indicator's flag is quote-grounded (verbatim) in the source md within the red-flag region (Phase 16). Coverage/data values are ILLUSTRATIVE (vision demo). FinCEN Alert, public domain (17 U.S.C. 105).

indicators.flag:
A customer in the maritime industry transports commodities of concern and uses trade
corridors known to serve as possible transshipment points21 for exports to Russia and Belarus.
indicators.red_flag: Commodities of concern routed via Russia/Belarus transshipment corridors
indicators.rationale: Detecting that a maritime customer routes commodities of concern through transshipment corridors needs trade-document and customs routing data the bank only partially holds.

indicators.flag:
The nature of a customer’s underlying business (specifically military or government-related
work), type of service(s) or product(s) offered, and geographical presence pose additional
risks of unintentional involvement in the evasion of export controls for Russia and Belarus.
indicators.red_flag: Military/government-related business with Russia/Belarus export-evasion exposure
indicators.rationale: Customer business-nature and geography are partly captured at KYC but military/government-relatedness needs external attribution to score reliably.

indicators.flag:
A customer acquires new vessels for no apparent economic or business purpose or for use in
shipping corridors involving one or more of the identified transshipment countries.
indicators.red_flag: No-purpose vessel acquisition into transshipment-country corridors
indicators.rationale: Vessel acquisition with no economic purpose is detectable from payment patterns but linking it to identified shipping corridors needs partial trade-routing data.

indicators.flag:
A customer purchases or sells vessels or other properties and goods identified as having been
involved with or being blocked property under U.S. or partner country sanctions.
indicators.red_flag: Dealing in sanctioned / blocked-property vessels or goods
indicators.rationale: Screening counterparties and property against sanctions/blocked-property lists is already standard coverage at a mid-size US bank.

indicators.flag: Transactions involving entities with little to no web presence.
indicators.red_flag: Counterparty with little-to-no web presence
indicators.rationale: Web-presence assessment of counterparties requires external open-source enrichment the bank does not currently hold.

indicators.flag:
Transactions involving a change in shipments or payments that were previously scheduled to
go to Russia or Belarus, or a company located in Russia or Belarus, but that are now going to a
different country/company.
indicators.red_flag: Russia/Belarus-bound shipment or payment rerouted to a new destination
indicators.rationale: A rerouting of previously Russia/Belarus-bound payments to a new country/company is detectable from the bank's own wire-payment history.

build_logic.logic: Flag a customer whose recent outbound payments redirect a previously scheduled Russia/Belarus (or Russia/Belarus-located company) destination to a different country or company within the lookback window.
build_logic.source: outbound wire/payment messages + historical beneficiary ledger
build_logic.route: Tier-1 alert → trade-finance sanctions review gate

indicators.flag:
Transactions involving payments being made from entities located in third-party countries not
otherwise involved with the transactions and known to be a potential transshipment point for
exports to Russia and Belarus.
indicators.red_flag: Third-party payer from a transshipment-point country, not party to the trade
indicators.rationale: Payments originating from unrelated third-party entities in known transshipment-point countries are visible in the bank's own payment-originator data.

build_logic.logic: Flag transactions where the paying entity sits in a known transshipment-point country and is not otherwise a party to the underlying trade relationship.
build_logic.source: inbound payment originator records + transshipment-country reference list

indicators.flag:
Last-minute changes to transactions associated with an originator or beneficiary located in
Russia or Belarus.
indicators.red_flag: Last-minute amendment on a Russia/Belarus-party transaction
indicators.rationale: Late amendments to transactions tied to a Russia/Belarus originator or beneficiary are observable directly from payment-message versioning the bank already records.

build_logic.logic: Flag transactions carrying last-minute amendments where the originator or beneficiary is located in Russia or Belarus.
build_logic.source: payment-message amendment/version log + party country attributes
build_logic.route: Tier-1 alert → sanctions amendment review gate

indicators.flag:
Parties to transactions with addresses that do not appear consistent with the business or are
otherwise problematic (e.g., either the physical address does not exist, or it is residential).
indicators.red_flag: Transaction-party address mismatch (non-existent / residential)
indicators.rationale: Party addresses are held by the bank and partly screened today; enhancing residential/non-existent-address detection sharpens an existing control.

indicators.flag:
Transactions involving consolidated shipments of luxury goods that previously would have
been destined for Russia or Belarus, but are now destined for a transshipment country or a
country without restrictions on exports/re-exports to Russia or Belarus.
indicators.red_flag: Luxury-goods consolidation rerouted off Russia/Belarus to a transshipment country
indicators.rationale: Identifying consolidated luxury-goods shipments rerouted away from Russia/Belarus needs trade-document and goods-classification data the bank only partially holds.

indicators.flag: Rapid shifts to new purchasers of transactions involving restricted luxury goods.
indicators.red_flag: Rapid purchaser churn on restricted luxury goods
indicators.rationale: A rapid turnover of purchasers on restricted-luxury-goods transactions is detectable from the bank's own counterparty and transaction history.

build_logic.logic: Flag accounts whose restricted-luxury-goods transactions show an abnormally high rate of switching to new purchasers within the window.
build_logic.source: transaction counterparty ledger + merchant/goods category tags
build_logic.route: Tier-1 alert → luxury-goods evasion review gate

indicators.flag:
Transactions involving freight-forwarding firms22 that are also listed as the product’s final end
customer, especially items going to traditional Russian transshipment hubs.
indicators.red_flag: Freight-forwarder doubling as the product's final end customer
indicators.rationale: Detecting a freight-forwarder posing as the final end customer needs trade-document end-user data the bank only partially holds.

indicators.flag: Transactions associated with atypical shipping routes for a product and destination.
indicators.red_flag: Atypical shipping route for the product and destination
indicators.rationale: Judging a shipping route as atypical for a product/destination requires trade-routing and customs data the bank only partially holds.

indicators.flag:
Transactions involving entities whose website or business registration states the entities work
on “special purpose projects.”23
indicators.red_flag: Counterparty advertising "special purpose projects" work
indicators.rationale: Reading a counterparty's website or business registration for 'special purpose projects' language requires external registry/open-source attribution the bank lacks.

indicators.flag:
Transactions involving companies that display a certificate from the Federal Security Service
of the Russian Federation (FSB RF), which allows these companies to work on projects
classified as a state secret.24
indicators.red_flag: Counterparty displaying an FSB RF state-secret certificate
indicators.rationale: Detecting an FSB RF state-secret certificate displayed by a company depends on external open-source/website attribution unavailable in bank data.

indicators.flag:
Transactions involving companies that are physically co-located with or have shared
ownership with an entity on the BIS Entity List25 or the Department of the Treasury’s Specially
Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List.26
indicators.red_flag: Co-location / shared ownership with a BIS Entity-List or SDN entity
indicators.rationale: SDN/Entity List screening is in place, but co-location and shared-ownership linkage needs external corporate-registry data only partially available.

indicators.flag:
New or existing accounts and transactions by individuals with previous convictions for
violating U.S. export control laws, particularly if appearing to involve export and import
activities or services.
indicators.red_flag: Account holder with prior export-control conviction in import/export activity
indicators.rationale: Tying account holders to prior export-control convictions requires external enforcement/conviction records the bank does not hold.

indicators.flag:
When combined with other derogatory information, large dollar or volume purchases,
including through the use of business credit cards, of items designated as EAR99 (or large
volume or dollar purchases at wholesale electrical/industrial merchants, electrical parts and
equipment providers, or electronic parts providers), in the United States or abroad, especially
if paired with purchases at shipping companies.
indicators.red_flag: Large EAR99 / electronics-parts card spend paired with shipping-company purchases
indicators.rationale: Large-volume electrical/industrial-parts purchases on business cards paired with shipping-company spend are fully visible in the bank's own card and merchant-category data.

build_logic.logic: Flag accounts with large-volume or large-dollar purchases at electrical/industrial/electronic-parts merchants paired with shipping-company spend in the same window.
build_logic.source: card transaction stream + merchant category codes

indicators.flag:
Companies or individuals with links to Russian state-owned corporations (including
shared ownership, as well as branches of, subsidiaries of, or shareholders in such
state-owned corporations) involved in export-related transactions or the provision of
export-related services.27
indicators.red_flag: Export ties to Russian state-owned corporations (shared ownership / subsidiary / shareholder)
indicators.rationale: Establishing ownership/shareholder links to Russian state-owned corporations requires external corporate-registry and beneficial-ownership data the bank lacks.

indicators.flag:
Export transactions identified through correspondent banking activities involving non-
U.S. parties that have shared owners or addresses with Russian state-owned entities or
designated companies.
indicators.red_flag: Correspondent-banking export flow sharing owners/addresses with Russian state-owned entities
indicators.rationale: Correspondent-banking export flows are visible, but shared-owner/address linkage to Russian state-owned entities needs partial external registry enrichment.

indicators.flag:
Use of business checking or foreign exchange accounts by U.S.-based merchants involved in
the import and export of electronic equipment where transactions are conducted with third-
country-based electronics and aerospace firms that also have offices in Russia or Belarus.
indicators.red_flag: Electronics merchant FX account transacting with Russia/Belarus-linked third-country firms
indicators.rationale: Business-checking/FX account flows of US electronics merchants transacting with third-country firms are observable in the bank's own account and counterparty data.

build_logic.logic: Flag US-based electronics import/export merchants whose business-checking or FX account activity is concentrated with third-country electronics/aerospace counterparties that also maintain Russia/Belarus offices.
build_logic.source: business-checking + FX account transactions and counterparty profiles

indicators.flag:
Transactions identified through correspondent banking activities connected to Russian
petroleum-related firms or firms that resell electronics and other similar items to Russian firms.
indicators.red_flag: Correspondent-banking flow to Russian petroleum or electronics-reseller firms
indicators.rationale: Correspondent-banking activity is visible, but attributing counterparties as Russian-petroleum or electronics-reseller firms needs partial external classification data.
